1.e4 d6 2.d4 e5 3.dxe5.strategy: Takes the pawn and offers a queen exchange: after Black recaptures, trading queens costs Black the right to castle and gives White a small lead in development. The endgame is easy to defend, so this gives White a pull and not more.

1.e4 d6 2.d4 e5 3.dxe5 Bd7.strategy: Sidesteps the queen exchange, but never wins back the pawn on e5, so Black is simply a pawn down. A developed bishop and some activity are poor payment for it.
1.e4 d6 2.d4 e5 3.dxe5 Bd7.name: King's Pawn Game: Philidor Gambit
